metadata.title: On asymptotically optimal confidence regions and tests for high-dimensional models
metadata.authors: Sara van de Geer, Peter Bühlmann, Ya'acov Ritov, Ruben Dezeure

nodes.name: High-dimensional linear model
nodes.statement: Linear model $Y = \bx \beta^0 + \eps$ with $n \times p$ design matrix $\bx$, Gaussian noise $\eps \sim \mathcal{N}_n(0, \sigma_\eps^2 I)$, $p > n$, active set $S_0 = \{j : \beta_j^0 \neq 0\}$ with cardinality $s_0 = |S_0|$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard high-dimensional linear regression model with sparse true parameter and sample size smaller than dimension.

nodes.name: Lasso estimator
nodes.statement: $\hat{\beta} = \hat{\beta}(\lambda) := \arg\min_{\beta \in \R^p} \bigl( \|Y - \bx \beta\|_2^2/n + 2 \lambda \|\beta\|_1 \bigr).$

nodes.name: KKT conditions for the lasso
nodes.statement: $-\bx^T(Y - \bx\hat\beta)/n + \lambda \hat\kappa = 0$, $\|\hat\kappa\|_\infty \le 1$, $\hat\kappa_j = \operatorname{sign}(\hat\beta_j)$ if $\hat\beta_j \neq 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: First-order optimality conditions for the lasso, with subgradient vector $\hat\kappa$.

nodes.name: Compatibility condition
nodes.statement: There exists $\phi_0 > 0$ such that for all $\beta$ with $\|\beta_{S_0^c}\|_1 \le 3 \|\beta_{S_0}\|_1$: $\|\beta_{S_0}\|_1^2 \le s_0 \beta^T \hat\Sigma \beta / \phi_0^2$. The constant $\phi_0^2$ is the compatibility constant.
nodes.statement_clean: Identifiability/restricted-eigenvalue-type condition on the design Gram matrix used to control lasso error in $\ell_1$ norm.

nodes.name: Desparsified lasso estimator
nodes.statement: $\hat{b} := \hat{\beta} + \hat{\Theta} \lambda \hat\kappa = \hat{\beta} + \hat{\Theta} \bx^T (Y - \bx \hat{\beta})/n$, where $\hat\Theta$ is an approximate inverse of $\hat\Sigma = \bx^T \bx / n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Bias-corrected estimator obtained by adding to $\hat\beta$ a relaxed-inverse of the empirical Gram matrix times the residual.

nodes.name: Nodewise lasso for approximate inverse
nodes.statement: For each $j$: $\hat\gamma_j := \arg\min_{\gamma \in \R^{p-1}} \bigl(\|X_j - \bx_{-j} \gamma\|_2^2/n + 2 \lambda_j \|\gamma\|_1\bigr)$; then $\hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}} := \hat T^{-2} \hat C$ with $\hat\tau_j^2 := \|X_j - \bx_{-j}\hat\gamma_j\|_2^2/n + \lambda_j \|\hat\gamma_j\|_1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Approximate inverse of the empirical Gram matrix obtained by performing $p$ separate lasso regressions of each column on the others.
nodes.origin_citation: Meinshausen & Bühlmann 2006 (introduced nodewise regression); formulation here adapts it

nodes.name: Extended KKT conditions
nodes.statement: For the nodewise lasso choice $\hat\Theta_j = \hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso},j}$: $\|\hat\Sigma \hat\Theta_j^T - e_j\|_\infty \le \lambda_j / \hat\tau_j^2$, where $e_j$ is the $j$th unit vector.
nodes.statement_clean: Bound on the error of the nodewise-lasso approximate inverse, derived from the nodewise lasso's KKT conditions.

nodes.name: Honest confidence intervals
nodes.statement: Confidence intervals for $\beta_j^0$ that achieve the nominal coverage uniformly over a class $\mathcal{B}(s_0)$ of sparse parameters: $\sup_{\beta^0 \in \mathcal{B}(s_0)} |\PP_{\beta^0}[\sqrt{n}(\hat b_{\mathrm{Lasso},j} - \beta_j^0)/(\sigma_\eps \sqrt{\hat\Omega_{j,j}}) \le z | \bx] - \Phi(z)| = o_\PP(1)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Confidence intervals whose coverage is asymptotically uniform over a sparse class of parameters.

nodes.name: $\ell_1$-penalized GLM estimator
nodes.statement: $\hat{\beta} = \arg\min_\beta (P_n \rho_\beta + \lambda \|\beta\|_1)$, where $\rho_\beta(y, x) = \rho(y, x\beta)$ is a strictly convex loss in $\beta$.
nodes.statement_clean: Regularized M-estimator with general convex loss for GLMs.

nodes.name: Desparsified GLM estimator
nodes.statement: $\hat{b} := \hat\beta - \hat\Theta P_n \dot\rho_{\hat\beta}$, with $\hat\Sigma := P_n \ddot\rho_{\hat\beta}$ and $\hat\Theta = \hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$ from nodewise lasso applied to $\hat\Sigma$.
nodes.statement_clean: Bias-corrected M-estimator that subtracts the score weighted by an approximate inverse Hessian.

nodes.name: Nodewise lasso with matrix input
nodes.statement: For matrix input $\hat\Sigma$ and each row $j$: $\hat\gamma_j := \arg\min_\gamma (\hat\Sigma_{j,j} - 2 \hat\Sigma_{j, \setminus j} \gamma + \gamma^T \hat\Sigma_{\setminus j, \setminus j} \gamma + 2\lambda_j \|\gamma\|_1)$, then $\hat\tau_j^2 = \hat\Sigma_{j,j} - \hat\Sigma_{j,\setminus j}\hat\gamma_j$.
nodes.statement_clean: Nodewise lasso generalized to take an arbitrary symmetric matrix as input rather than $\bx^T \bx/n$.

nodes.name: Assumption (A1) — compatibility for fixed design
nodes.statement: (A1) The compatibility condition holds for $\hat\Sigma$ with constant $\phi_0^2 > 0$. Furthermore, $\max_j \hat\Sigma_{j,j} \le M^2$ for some $0 < M < \infty$.

nodes.name: Assumption (A2) — Gaussian random design
nodes.statement: (A2) Rows of $\bx$ are i.i.d. Gaussian with population inner product matrix $\Sigma$, smallest eigenvalue $\Lambda_{\min}^2$ satisfying $1/\Lambda_{\min}^2 = \mathcal O(1)$, and $\max_j \Sigma_{j,j} = \mathcal O(1)$.

nodes.name: Assumptions (B1)–(B4) — sub-Gaussian/bounded design
nodes.statement: (B1) Sub-Gaussian or (strongly) bounded rows of $\bx$. (B2) Sparsity: $\max_j \sqrt{s_j \log p / n} = o(1)$ (sub-Gaussian) or $\max_j K^2 s_j \sqrt{\log p / n} = o(1)$ (bounded). (B3) $1/\Lambda_{\min}^2 = \mathcal O(1)$ and $\max_j \Sigma_{j,j} = \mathcal O(1)$. (B4) In the bounded case, $\max_j \EE \eta_{1,j}^4 = \mathcal O(K^4)$.

nodes.name: Assumptions (C1)–(C8) — GLM regularity
nodes.statement: (C1) Lipschitz $\ddot\rho$, bounded $\dot\rho_{\beta^0}$ and $\ddot\rho$ near $\beta^0$. (C2) Lasso rates $\|\hat\beta-\beta^0\|_1 = \mathcal O_\PP(s_0 \lambda)$, etc. (C3) $\|\bx\|_\infty = \mathcal O(K)$. (C4) $\|P_n\ddot\rho_{\hat\beta}\hat\Theta_j^T - e_j\|_\infty = \mathcal O_\PP(\lambda_*)$. (C5) $\|\bx\hat\Theta_j^T\|_\infty=\mathcal O_\PP(K)$, $\|\hat\Theta_j\|_1 = \mathcal O_\PP(\sqrt{s_*})$. (C6) Concentration of $(P_n-P)\dot\rho\dot\rho^T$. (C7) CLT for $\sqrt n (\hat\Theta P_n \dot\rho_{\beta^0})_j / \sqrt{(\hat\Theta P\dot\rho\dot\rho^T \hat\Theta^T)_{j,j}}$. (C8) $K s_0 \lambda^2 = o(n^{-1/2})$, $\lambda_* \lambda s_0 = o(n^{-1/2})$, $K^2 s_* \lambda + K^2\sqrt{s_0}\lambda = o(1)$.

nodes.name: Assumptions (D1)–(D5) — nodewise regression for random matrices
nodes.statement: (D1) $(y_i,x_i)$ i.i.d., $\|\bx\|_\infty = \mathcal O(K)$, $\|\bx_{\beta^0,-j}\gamma_{\beta^0,j}\|_\infty = \mathcal O(K)$. (D2) $K^2 s_j \sqrt{\log p / n} = o(1)$. (D3) $1/\Lambda_{\min}^2 = \mathcal O(1)$, $\|\Sigma_{\beta^0}\|_\infty = \mathcal O(1)$. (D4) Weights $w_\beta$ stay away from zero, are bounded, and Lipschitz in $\beta$. (D5) $\|\bx(\hat\beta-\beta^0)\|_n = \mathcal O_\PP(\lambda \sqrt{s_0})$, $\|\hat\beta - \beta^0\|_1 = \mathcal O_\PP(\lambda s_0)$.

nodes.name: Pivot identity
nodes.statement: $\hat\beta - \beta^0 + \hat\Theta \lambda \hat\kappa = \hat\Theta \bx^T \eps / n - \Delta/\sqrt n$, where $\Delta := \sqrt n (\hat\Theta \hat\Sigma - I)(\hat\beta - \beta^0)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Decomposition expressing the desparsified estimator's error as a Gaussian-like term plus a remainder $\Delta$.

nodes.name: Asymptotic pivot
nodes.statement: $\sqrt{n}(\hat b - \beta^0) = W + o_\PP(1)$, $W | \bx \sim \mathcal N_p(0, \sigma_\eps^2 \hat\Theta\hat\Sigma\hat\Theta^T)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Asymptotic Gaussian representation of the desparsified lasso estimator when the remainder is negligible.

nodes.name: Nodewise lasso algorithm
nodes.statement: Compute approximate inverse $\hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$ of $\hat\Sigma = \bx^T\bx/n$ via $p$ lasso regressions of each $X_j$ on $\bx_{-j}$.

nodes.name: Desparsified lasso (Lasso-Pro) procedure for linear models
nodes.statement: Compute $\hat\beta$ by lasso, compute $\hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$ by nodewise lasso, then return $\hat b_{\mathrm{Lasso}} = \hat\beta + \hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}} \bx^T (Y - \bx\hat\beta)/n$ and confidence intervals $\hat b_j \pm \Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2) \sigma_\eps \sqrt{(\hat\Theta\hat\Sigma\hat\Theta^T)_{j,j}/n}$.

nodes.name: Desparsified GLM (Lasso-ProG) procedure
nodes.statement: Compute $\hat\beta$ minimizing $P_n \rho_\beta + \lambda\|\beta\|_1$, build $\hat\Sigma = P_n \ddot\rho_{\hat\beta}$, run nodewise lasso to get $\hat\Theta$, then return $\hat b = \hat\beta - \hat\Theta P_n \dot\rho_{\hat\beta}$ with standard errors $\hat\sigma_j^2 = (\hat\Theta P_n \dot\rho_{\hat\beta}\dot\rho_{\hat\beta}^T \hat\Theta^T)_{j,j}$.
output: Asymptotic standard errors $\hat\sigma_j$ and confidence intervals/$p$-values

nodes.name: Theorem 2.1 — Decomposition for fixed design
nodes.statement: $\sqrt n (\hat b_{\mathrm{Lasso}} - \beta^0) = W + \Delta$, $W = \hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}} \bx^T \eps/\sqrt n \sim \mathcal N_n(0, \sigma_\eps^2 \hat\Omega)$ with $\hat\Omega := \hat\Theta\hat\Sigma\hat\Theta^T$, and $\PP[\|\Delta\|_\infty \ge 8\sqrt n (\max_j \lambda_j/\hat\tau_j^2)\lambda s_0/\phi_0^2] \le 2 \exp[-t^2]$.
assumptions: Linear model (\ref{modlin}) with Gaussian errors $\eps \sim \mathcal N_n(0, \sigma_\eps^2 I)$
conclusions: Decomposition $\sqrt n (\hat b_{\mathrm{Lasso}} - \beta^0) = W + \Delta$ with $W$ exactly Gaussian conditional on $\bx$

nodes.name: Theorem 2.2 — Asymptotic pivot for Gaussian random design
nodes.statement: Under random Gaussian design (A2) and sparsity $s_0 = o(\sqrt n / \log p)$, $\max_j s_j = o(n/\log p)$, with $\lambda \asymp \lambda_j \asymp \sqrt{\log p/n}$: $\sqrt n (\hat b_{\mathrm{Lasso}} - \beta^0) = W + \Delta$, $W|\bx \sim \mathcal N_p(0, \sigma_\eps^2 \hat\Omega)$, $\|\Delta\|_\infty = o_\PP(1)$, and $\|\hat\Omega - \Sigma^{-1}\|_\infty = o_\PP(1)$.
assumptions: Linear model (\ref{modlin}) with Gaussian errors and $\sigma_\eps^2 = \mathcal O(1)$
$s_0 = o(\sqrt n / \log p)$ and $\max_j s_j = o(n / \log p)$
$\lambda \asymp \sqrt{\log p / n}$ and $\lambda_j \asymp \sqrt{\log p / n}$ uniformly in $j$
conclusions: $\sqrt n (\hat b_{\mathrm{Lasso}} - \beta^0) = W + \Delta$ with $W | \bx$ exactly Gaussian

nodes.name: Corollary 2.1 — Honest convergence uniform over sparse class
nodes.statement: Under (A2) and $\beta^0 \in \mathcal B(s_0)$ with $s_0 = o(\sqrt n/\log p)$, $\max_j s_j = o(n/\log p)$, the conclusion of Theorem 2.2 holds with $\|\Delta\|_\infty = o_{\PP_{\beta^0}}(1)$ uniformly in $\beta^0 \in \mathcal B(s_0)$.
conclusions: Decomposition $\sqrt n (\hat b_{\mathrm{Lasso}} - \beta^0) = W + \Delta$ holds with $\|\Delta\|_\infty = o_{\PP_{\beta^0}}(1)$ uniformly in $\beta^0 \in \mathcal B(s_0)$
Uniform convergence of CDFs: $\sup_{\beta^0} |\PP_{\beta^0}[\sqrt n (\hat b_{\mathrm{Lasso},j} - \beta_j^0)/(\sigma_\eps \sqrt{\hat\Omega_{j,j}}) \le z | \bx] - \Phi(z)| = o_\PP(1)$

nodes.name: Theorem 2.3 — Semiparametric efficiency
nodes.statement: Under (\ref{asyEff}) and the conditions of Theorem TP20.2, $\hat b_{\mathrm{Lasso};1} = \beta_1^0 + n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n (X_{i,1} - \EE[X_{i,1}|Z_i])\eps_i + o_\PP(n^{-1/2})$, and the limiting variance of $\sqrt n (\hat b_{\mathrm{Lasso};1} - \beta_1^0)$ reaches the information bound $\sigma_\eps^2/\EE(X_{1,1} - \EE[X_{1,1}|Z_1])^2$. Moreover $\hat b_{\mathrm{Lasso};1}$ is regular and asymptotically efficient for $\beta_1^0$.
conclusions: Limiting variance equals the semiparametric information bound
$\hat b_{\mathrm{Lasso};1}$ is regular and asymptotically efficient

nodes.name: Lemma 2.1 — Concrete example satisfies (\ref{asyEff})
nodes.statement: In the partially linear example (\ref{modsemip}), the asymptotic representation condition (\ref{asyEff}) is satisfied.
assumptions: Setting (\ref{modsemip}): infinite-dimensional sparse linear representation of $K(Z_1)$, $\beta^0 \in \mathcal B(s_0)$ with finite $s_0$, finite-variance covariates, positive definite covariance function, and a finite-support population projection $\gamma_1$
conclusions: Condition (\ref{asyEff}) holds in this concrete example

nodes.name: Theorem 2.4 — Nodewise lasso under sub-Gaussian/bounded design
nodes.statement: Under (B1)–(B4), with $\lambda_j \asymp K_0 \sqrt{\log p/n}$: $\|\hat\Theta_j - \Theta_j\|_1 = \mathcal O_\PP(K_0 s_j \sqrt{\log p/n})$, $\|\hat\Theta_j - \Theta_j\|_2 = \mathcal O_\PP(K_0 \sqrt{s_j \log p / n})$, $|\hat\tau_j^2 - \tau_j^2| = \mathcal O_\PP(K_0 \sqrt{s_j \log p/n})$. Furthermore, $\sqrt n(\hat b_{\mathrm{Lasso}} - \beta^0) = W + \Delta$ with $W = \hat\Theta\bx^T \varepsilon/\sqrt n$ and $|\Delta_j| = o_\PP(1)$ for all $j$ (uniformly in the sub-Gaussian or strongly bounded case).
assumptions: Errors i.i.d. with $\sigma_\eps^2 = \mathcal O(1)$, sub-exponential in the sub-Gaussian design case
Tuning $\lambda \asymp K_0 \sqrt{\log p/n}$ and $\lambda_j \asymp K_0 \sqrt{\log p/n}$
$K_0 s_0 \log p / \sqrt n = o(1)$ and $\max_j K_0 s_j \sqrt{\log p/n} = o(1)$

nodes.name: Theorem 3.1 — Asymptotic normality of desparsified GLM estimator
nodes.statement: $\sqrt n (\hat b_j - \beta_j^0)/\hat\sigma_j = V_j + o_\PP(1)$, with $V_j$ converging weakly to $\mathcal N(0,1)$, where $\hat\sigma_j^2 := (\hat\Theta P_n \dot\rho_{\hat\beta} \dot\rho_{\hat\beta}^T \hat\Theta^T)_{j,j}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.2 — Nodewise regression for GLM-style random matrices
nodes.statement: Under (D1)–(D5) with $\lambda_j \asymp K\sqrt{\log p/n}$: $\|\hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j} - \Theta_{\beta^0,j}\|_1 = \mathcal O_\PP(K s_j \sqrt{\log p/n}) + \mathcal O_\PP(K^2 s_0 ((\lambda^2/\sqrt{\log p/n}) \vee \lambda))$, with analogous bounds for $\|\cdot\|_2$ and $|\hat\tau^2 - \tau^2|$. Moreover, $|\hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j}\Sigma_{\beta^0}\hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j}^T - \Theta_{\beta^0,j,j}|$ is bounded by the corresponding $\ell_1$ or $\ell_2$ error plus $2|\hat\tau^2 - \tau^2|$.
conclusions: Estimation-error rates for nodewise lasso applied to weighted-design Gram matrix

nodes.name: Corollary 3.1 — Negligibility of nodewise-regression errors for GLM
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Theorem TP20.6 with $\lambda \asymp \sqrt{\log p/n}$, $K \asymp 1$, $s_j = o(\sqrt n / \log p)$ and $s_0 = o(\sqrt n / \log p)$: $\|\hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j} - \Theta_{\beta^0,j}\|_1 = o_\PP(1/\sqrt{\log p})$, $\|\hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j} - \Theta_{\beta^0,j}\|_2 = o_\PP(n^{-1/4})$ and $|\hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j}\Sigma_{\beta^0}\hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j}^T - \Theta_{\beta^0,j,j}| = o_\PP(1/\log p)$.
assumptions: Conditions of Theorem TP20.6 with $K \asymp 1$, $\lambda \asymp \sqrt{\log p/n}$, $s_j = o(\sqrt n / \log p)$, $s_0 = o(\sqrt n / \log p)$
conclusions: Negligibility rates for $\|\hat\Theta - \Theta\|_1$, $\|\hat\Theta - \Theta\|_2$, and the variance estimate

nodes.name: Lemma 3.1 — Asymptotic-variance lemma
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Corollary CP20.2, with $(x_i, \xi_i)$ i.i.d., $\EE x_i^T \xi_i = 0$, $|\xi_i| \le 1$: $\hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j}\sum_i x_i^T \xi_i / n = \Theta_{\beta^0,j} \sum_i x_i^T \xi_i/n + o_\PP(n^{-1/2})$. With $A := \EE x_i^T x_i \xi_i^2$ satisfying $\|A\Theta_j^T\|_\infty = \mathcal O(1)$ and $1/(\Theta_j A \Theta_j^T) = \mathcal O(1)$: $\hat\Theta A \hat\Theta^T = \Theta A \Theta^T + o_\PP(1)$ and $\hat\Theta\sum_i x_i^T \xi_i/\sqrt n / \sqrt{\hat\Theta A \hat\Theta^T}$ converges weakly to $\mathcal N(0,1)$.
conclusions: Score representation $\hat\Theta P_n x^T \xi = \Theta P_n x^T \xi + o_\PP(n^{-1/2})$

nodes.name: Theorem 3.3 — Asymptotic normality for GLMs with bounded design
nodes.statement: Under (i)–(vii) (Lipschitz $\ddot\rho$, bounded inverse second derivative, $\|\bx\|_\infty = \mathcal O(1)$, bounded $\bx\beta^0$ and projection, smallest eigenvalue of $\Sigma_{\beta^0}$ bounded away from zero, bounded $1/(\Theta_{\beta^0,j} P\dot\rho\dot\rho^T \Theta_{\beta^0,j}^T)$, and $s_0, s_j = o(\sqrt n / \log p)$), with $\hat\Theta = \hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$ from (\ref{nodelassoglm}) and $\lambda_j, \lambda \asymp \sqrt{\log p / n}$: $\sqrt n (\hat b_j - \beta_j^0)/\hat\sigma_j = V_j + o_\PP(1)$ with $V_j \stackrel{d}{\to} \mathcal N(0,1)$.
assumptions: (v) Smallest eigenvalue of $\Sigma_{\beta^0}$ stays away from zero
(vii) $s_0 = o(\sqrt n / \log p)$ and $s_j = o(\sqrt{n/\log p})$

nodes.name: Remark 2.1 — Studentized version
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Theorem TP20.1: $\sqrt n (\hat b_{\mathrm{Lasso},j} - \beta_j^0)/(\hat\Omega_{j,j}^{1/2}\sigma_\eps) = V_j + \tilde\Delta_j$ with $V_j \sim \mathcal N(0,1)$ and a probability bound on $|\tilde\Delta_j|$. Studentization replaces $\sigma_\eps^2$ by a consistent estimator $\tilde\sigma_\eps^2$, e.g. via the square-root lasso of Belloni et al. 2011.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.1 — $\ell_1$-bound for the lasso (fixed design)
nodes.statement: $\|\hat\beta - \beta^0\|_1 \le 8\lambda s_0/\phi_0^2$ and $\|\bx(\hat\beta - \beta^0)\|_2^2/n \le 8\lambda^2 s_0/\phi_0^2$ with probability at least $1 - 2\exp(-t^2)$.
assumptions: Linear model with Gaussian errors and fixed design $\bx$
Compatibility condition with constant $\phi_0^2$ and $\hat\Sigma_{j,j} \le M^2$

nodes.name: Lemma 5.2 — Compatibility under (A2)
nodes.statement: Under (A2) and $s_0 = o(n/\log p)$, with probability tending to one the compatibility condition holds with constant $\phi_0^2 \ge 1/L^2$ for some $L = \mathcal O(1)$ depending on $\Lambda_{\min}$.
conclusions: Compatibility condition holds w.h.p. with $\phi_0^2 \ge 1/L^2$, $L = \mathcal O(1)$

nodes.name: Lemma 5.3 — Boundedness of $1/\hat\tau_j^2$
nodes.statement: Under (A2) and $\max_j s_j = o(n/\log p)$, with $\lambda_j \asymp \sqrt{\log p/n}$: $\max_j 1/\hat\tau_j^2 = \mathcal O_\PP(1)$.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.4 — Consistency of $\hat\Omega$
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Lemma LP20.5 and $\max_j \lambda_j^2 s_j = o(1)$: $\|\hat\Omega - \Theta\|_\infty = o_\PP(1)$.

nodes.name: Riboflavin (vitamin $B_2$) production data
nodes.statement: Real-data analysis on a riboflavin-production dataset with $n = 71$ samples of bacillus subtilis and $p = 4088$ gene-expression covariates: the desparsified lasso finds no significant coefficient at FWER $0.05$ while multiple sample splitting flags one variable.
nodes.statement_clean: High-dimensional gene-expression dataset used to illustrate the desparsified lasso for inference.

nodes.name: Simulation study with Toeplitz and equi-correlated designs
nodes.statement: Simulations with $n = 100$, $p = 500$, Gaussian designs with covariance either Toeplitz $\Sigma_{j,k} = 0.9^{|j-k|}$ or equi-correlated $\Sigma_{j,k} \equiv 0.8$ ($j\neq k$), $s_0 \in \{3, 15\}$, comparing Lasso-Pro, residual bootstrap and multiple sample splitting in terms of coverage, length, FWER and power.
nodes.statement_clean: Synthetic-data benchmark comparing the desparsified lasso to a residual bootstrap and to multiple sample splitting.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.1
nodes.statement: From the bound $\|\Delta\|_\infty/\sqrt n \le \|(\hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}}\hat\Sigma - I)\|_\infty \|\hat\beta - \beta^0\|_1$, the extended KKT bound (\ref{add-inver}), and Lemma LP20.3.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.2
nodes.statement: Combine Theorem TP20.1 and Lemma LP20.5 to obtain $\|\Delta\|_\infty = \mathcal O_\PP(s_0 \log p / \sqrt n) = o_\PP(1)$, then invoke Lemma LP20.6 for $\|\hat\Omega - \Theta\|_\infty = o_\PP(1)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.4
nodes.statement: Establish sub-Gaussian/bounded concentration of $\eta_j^T\bx_{-j}/n$, derive empirical compatibility, then control $\|\hat\gamma_j - \gamma_j\|_2$ and $|\hat\tau_j^2 - \tau_j^2|$ via decomposition into four terms; combine to bound $\|\hat\Theta_j - \Theta_j\|_1$ and $\|\cdot\|_2$ and conclude the pivot decomposition.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.1
nodes.statement: Taylor-expand $\dot\rho_{\hat\beta}$ around $\beta^0$, control the remainder using (C1)–(C2), use (C4) to bound $\|\hat\Theta_j P_n \ddot\rho_{\hat\beta} - e_j^T\|_\infty$, and verify variance consistency via (C5)–(C8); then invoke (C7) for the CLT.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3
nodes.statement: Verify (C2) via the compatibility condition implied by (i)–(v), check (C3) directly, deduce (C4)–(C7) from Corollary CP20.2 and Lemma LP20.2 with $\Sigma_\beta = P\ddot\rho_\beta$, then apply Theorem TP20.5.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.3
nodes.statement: Use union-bound compatibility from Lemma LP20.4 across all nodewise regressions, the bound $\tau_j^2 \ge \Lambda_{\min}^2 > 0$, and the lasso $\ell_1$-rate to show $\hat\tau_j^2 = \tau_j^2 + o_\PP(1)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.4
nodes.statement: Decompose $\hat\Omega = (\hat\Theta\hat\Sigma - I)\hat\Theta^T + \hat\Theta^T$; bound the first term via the extended KKT (\ref{add-inver}) and Lemma LP20.5; bound $\|\hat\Theta - \Theta\|_\infty$ via $\ell_2$-rates.

nodes.name: Bound $\|\Delta\|_\infty$ by Hölder
nodes.statement: From $\Delta = \sqrt n (\hat\Theta\hat\Sigma - I)(\hat\beta - \beta^0)$: $\|\Delta\|_\infty/\sqrt n \le \|\hat\Theta\hat\Sigma - I\|_\infty \|\hat\beta - \beta^0\|_1$.

nodes.name: Apply extended KKT to control $\|\hat\Theta\hat\Sigma - I\|_\infty$
nodes.statement: By the extended KKT bound (\ref{add-inver}): $\|\hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}}\hat\Sigma - I\|_\infty \le \max_j \lambda_j/\hat\tau_j^2$.

nodes.name: Plug in lasso $\ell_1$-bound
nodes.statement: Substitute the Lemma LP20.3 bound $\|\hat\beta - \beta^0\|_1 \le 8\lambda s_0/\phi_0^2$ to obtain the probabilistic bound on $\|\Delta\|_\infty$.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem TP20.1 + Lemma LP20.5 to bound $\|\Delta\|_\infty$
nodes.statement: By TP20.1, $\|\Delta\|_\infty \le \sqrt n \|\hat\beta - \beta^0\|_1 \max_j \lambda_j/\hat\tau_j^2$; combined with Lemma LP20.5 ($\max_j 1/\hat\tau_j^2 = \mathcal O_\PP(1)$) and the lasso $\ell_1$-rate (\ref{ell1-bound}): $\|\Delta\|_\infty = \mathcal O_\PP(s_0 \log p / \sqrt n)$.

nodes.name: Use sparsity to make remainder negligible
nodes.statement: Sparsity assumption $s_0 = o(\sqrt n / \log p)$ implies $s_0 \log p / \sqrt n = o(1)$, hence $\|\Delta\|_\infty = o_\PP(1)$.

nodes.name: Variance-matrix consistency via Lemma LP20.6
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma LP20.6 to obtain $\|\hat\Omega - \Theta\|_\infty = o_\PP(1)$, completing the proof.

nodes.name: Concentration of $\eta_j^T \bx_{-j}/n$
nodes.statement: Sub-Gaussianity of $\eta_j$ gives $\|\eta_j^T\bx_{-j}/n\|_\infty = \mathcal O_\PP(\sqrt{\log p/n})$ in the sub-Gaussian case; in the strongly bounded case use the Duembgen-style bound to get $\mathcal O_\PP(K\sqrt{\log p/n})$ uniformly in $j$.

nodes.name: Empirical compatibility for nodewise regressions
nodes.statement: Use $K^2 s_j \sqrt{\log p/n} = o(1)$ in the bounded case (Section 6.12 of Bühlmann & van de Geer 2011) and a sub-Gaussian extension of Raskutti et al. 2010 in the sub-Gaussian case to deduce empirical compatibility for nodewise regressions of $X_j$ on $\bx_{-j}$.

nodes.name: Rates for $\|\hat\gamma_j - \gamma_j\|_1$ and $\|\hat\gamma_j - \gamma_j\|_2$
nodes.statement: Standard lasso analysis applied to the nodewise regression yields $\|\hat\gamma_j - \gamma_j\|_1 = \mathcal O_\PP(s_j \lambda_j)$, $\|\bx_{-j}(\hat\gamma_j - \gamma_j)\|_n^2 = \mathcal O_\PP(s_j \lambda_j^2)$, $\|\hat\gamma_j - \gamma_j\|_2 = \mathcal O_\PP(K_0 \sqrt{s_j\log p/n})$.

nodes.name: Decompose and bound $|\hat\tau_j^2 - \tau_j^2|$
nodes.statement: Write $|\hat\tau_j^2 - \tau_j^2|$ as a sum of four terms $I + II + III + IV$ and bound each using the rates above plus the KKT conditions for nodewise regression to get $|\hat\tau_j^2 - \tau_j^2| = \mathcal O_\PP(K_0 \sqrt{s_j \log p/n})$.

nodes.name: Combine into $\|\hat\Theta_j - \Theta_j\|_1$ and $\|\cdot\|_2$
nodes.statement: Using $\hat\Theta_j = \hat C_j/\hat\tau_j^2$ and the bounds above: $\|\hat\Theta_j - \Theta_j\|_1 = \mathcal O_\PP(K_0 s_j \sqrt{\log p/n})$ and $\|\hat\Theta_j - \Theta_j\|_2 = \mathcal O_\PP(K_0 \sqrt{s_j \log p/n})$.

nodes.name: Pivot remainder $\Delta_j$ is negligible
nodes.statement: By an analogue of Theorem TP20.1: $\Delta_j \le \sqrt n \lambda_j/\hat\tau_j^2 \|\hat\beta - \beta^0\|_1$, and the choice $\lambda_j/\hat\tau_j^2 \asymp \sqrt{\log p/n}$ together with $K_0 s_0 \log p/\sqrt n = o(1)$ gives $|\Delta_j| = o_\PP(1)$.

nodes.name: Taylor-expand the score
nodes.statement: $\dot\rho(y, x_i\hat\beta) = \dot\rho(y, x_i\beta^0) + \ddot\rho(y,\tilde a_i) x_i (\hat\beta - \beta^0)$ for some intermediate $\tilde a_i$.

nodes.name: Bound the Lipschitz remainder
nodes.statement: By (C1) Lipschitz $\ddot\rho$, the difference between $\ddot\rho(y,\tilde a_i)$ and $\ddot\rho(y,x_i\hat\beta)$ is bounded by $|x_i(\hat\beta - \beta^0)|$, yielding $\mathrm{Rem}_1 = \mathcal O_\PP(K s_0 \lambda^2) = o_\PP(1)$ via (C2) and (C8).

nodes.name: Use (C4) to identify the bias term
nodes.statement: By (C4) $\|\hat\Theta_j P_n \ddot\rho_{\hat\beta} - e_j^T\|_\infty = \mathcal O(\lambda_*)$, hence the bias $|(\hat\Theta_j P_n \ddot\rho_{\hat\beta} - e_j^T)(\hat\beta - \beta^0)| = \mathcal O_\PP(\lambda_* s_0 \lambda) = o_\PP(n^{-1/2})$.

nodes.name: Linearize the desparsified estimator
nodes.statement: Combining the previous steps yields $\hat b_j - \beta_j^0 = -\hat\Theta_j P_n \dot\rho_{\beta^0} - \mathrm{Rem}_2$ with $|\mathrm{Rem}_2| = o_\PP(n^{-1/2})$.

nodes.name: Variance estimate consistency
nodes.statement: Decompose the variance error into terms $I$ (empirical-process error) and $II$ (loss-function perturbation); bound each by $\mathcal O_\PP(K^2 s_* \lambda)$ and $\mathcal O_\PP(K^2 \sqrt{s_0}\lambda)$ respectively via (C5)–(C6), giving $I + II = o_\PP(1)$ by (C8).

nodes.name: Invoke CLT (C7)
nodes.statement: Condition (C7) gives weak convergence $V_j \to \mathcal N(0,1)$ for the studentized score, completing the proof.

nodes.name: Verify (C2) via compatibility from (v)
nodes.statement: Use $\|\hat\Sigma - \Sigma_{\beta^0}\|_\infty = \mathcal O_\PP(\lambda_*)$ and the smallest-eigenvalue assumption to conclude the compatibility condition for the GLM-design matrix.

nodes.name: Verify (C4) via Theorem TP20.6 / Corollary CP20.2
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem TP20.6 / Corollary CP20.2 to the matrix input $\hat\Sigma$ to deduce $\|P_n\ddot\rho_{\hat\beta}\hat\Theta_j^T - e_j\|_\infty = \mathcal O_\PP(\sqrt{\log p/n})$.

nodes.name: Verify (C5)–(C6)
nodes.statement: $\|\Theta_{\beta^0,j}\|_1 = \mathcal O(\sqrt{s_j})$ and the rate from Corollary CP20.2 give $\|\hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j}\|_1 = \mathcal O_\PP(\sqrt{s_j})$. (C6) follows from boundedness of $\dot\rho_{\beta^0}$ and $\|\bx\|_\infty = \mathcal O(1)$.

nodes.name: Verify (C7) via Lemma LP20.2
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma LP20.2 (with $\xi$ taken as $\dot\rho/\dot\rho$-normalized score) to obtain CLT (C7).

nodes.name: Apply Theorem TP20.5
nodes.statement: All assumptions of Theorem TP20.5 are met, hence $\sqrt n (\hat b_j - \beta_j^0)/\hat\sigma_j \stackrel{d}{\to} \mathcal N(0,1)$.

nodes.name: Uniform compatibility for nodewise regressions
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma LP20.4 with a union bound across all $p$ nodewise regressions to obtain the compatibility condition uniformly in $j$ with constant bounded away from zero.

nodes.name: Bound population error variance $\tau_j^2$
nodes.statement: $\tau_j^2 = 1/\Theta_{j,j} \ge \Lambda_{\min}^2 > 0$ and $\tau_j^2 \le \Sigma_{j,j} = \mathcal O(1)$ uniformly in $j$ by (A2).

nodes.name: Approximate $\hat\tau_j^2$ by $\tau_j^2$
nodes.statement: Decomposition $\hat\tau_j^2 = \|X_j - \bx_{-j}\hat\gamma_j\|_2^2/n + \lambda_j\|\hat\gamma_j\|_1 = \tau_j^2 + o_\PP(1)$ via standard lasso $\ell_1$-rate and $\|\gamma_j\|_1 \le \sqrt{s_j \Sigma_{j,j}}/\Lambda_{\min}$.

nodes.name: Conclude $\max_j 1/\hat\tau_j^2 = \mathcal O_\PP(1)$
nodes.statement: Combining the lower bound on $\tau_j^2$ with the consistency of $\hat\tau_j^2$ gives $\max_j 1/\hat\tau_j^2 = \mathcal O_\PP(1)$.

nodes.name: Decompose $\hat\Omega$
nodes.statement: $\hat\Omega = \hat\Theta\hat\Sigma\hat\Theta^T = (\hat\Theta\hat\Sigma - I)\hat\Theta^T + \hat\Theta^T$.

nodes.name: Bound $\|(\hat\Theta\hat\Sigma - I)\hat\Theta^T\|_\infty$
nodes.statement: By the extended KKT bound: $\|(\hat\Theta\hat\Sigma - I)\hat\Theta^T\|_\infty \le \max_j \lambda_j \|\hat\Theta_j\|_1/\hat\tau_j^2 = o_\PP(1)$ (using Lemma LP20.5 and $\|\hat\Theta_j\|_1 = \mathcal O_\PP(\sqrt{s_j})$).

nodes.name: Bound $\|\hat\Theta - \Theta\|_\infty$ via $\ell_2$-rate
nodes.statement: Standard $\ell_2$-rate arguments give $\|\hat\Theta - \Theta\|_\infty \le \max_j \|\hat\Theta_j - \Theta_j\|_2 \le \max_j \lambda_j\sqrt{s_j} = o_\PP(1)$.

nodes.name: Combine to conclude
nodes.statement: The two bounds plus the decomposition give $\|\hat\Omega - \Theta\|_\infty = o_\PP(1)$.

nodes.name: Loop over coordinates $j$
nodes.statement: For each $j = 1, \ldots, p$, compute $\hat\gamma_j = \arg\min_\gamma (\|X_j - \bx_{-j}\gamma\|_2^2/n + 2\lambda_j \|\gamma\|_1)$.

nodes.name: Compute residual variances
nodes.statement: Compute $\hat\tau_j^2 = \|X_j - \bx_{-j}\hat\gamma_j\|_2^2/n + \lambda_j \|\hat\gamma_j\|_1$ for each $j$.

nodes.name: Assemble $\hat C$ and return $\hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$
nodes.statement: Form the $p \times p$ matrix $\hat C$ with $(j,k)$-entry $-\hat\gamma_{j,k}$ off the diagonal and $1$ on the diagonal, and $\hat T^2 = \operatorname{diag}(\hat\tau_1^2, \ldots, \hat\tau_p^2)$; return $\hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}} = \hat T^{-2}\hat C$.

nodes.name: Compute lasso $\hat\beta$
nodes.statement: Solve $\hat\beta = \arg\min_\beta (\|Y - \bx\beta\|_2^2/n + 2\lambda\|\beta\|_1)$ with $\lambda \asymp \sqrt{\log p/n}$ (e.g. via the scaled lasso to also estimate $\sigma_\eps$).

nodes.name: Compute approximate inverse $\hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$
nodes.statement: Run the nodewise lasso algorithm AP20.1 on $\bx$ with tuning $\lambda_j \asymp \sqrt{\log p/n}$.

nodes.name: Form desparsified estimator and confidence intervals
nodes.statement: Return $\hat b_{\mathrm{Lasso}} = \hat\beta + \hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}}\bx^T(Y - \bx\hat\beta)/n$ and intervals $[\hat b_j \pm \Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\hat\sigma_\eps \sqrt{(\hat\Theta\hat\Sigma\hat\Theta^T)_{j,j}/n}]$.

nodes.name: Compute $\ell_1$-penalized GLM estimate
nodes.statement: Solve $\hat\beta = \arg\min_\beta (P_n \rho_\beta + \lambda\|\beta\|_1)$ with $\lambda \asymp \sqrt{\log p/n}$ (e.g. via lasso with cross-validated tuning for logistic regression).

nodes.name: Compute weighted Gram matrix
nodes.statement: Form $\hat\Sigma = P_n \ddot\rho_{\hat\beta}$; for canonical-link GLMs, write it as $\bx_{\hat\beta}^T \bx_{\hat\beta}/n$ with $\bx_{\hat\beta} = W_{\hat\beta}\bx$ and weights $w_{i,\hat\beta} = \sqrt{\ddot\rho(y_i, x_i\hat\beta)}$.

nodes.name: Run nodewise lasso on $\hat\Sigma$
nodes.statement: Use Algorithm AP20.1 (or its matrix-input variant) on $\hat\Sigma$ to compute $\hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$ and $\hat\tau_j^2$.

nodes.name: Form desparsified estimator and standard errors
nodes.statement: Return $\hat b = \hat\beta - \hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}} P_n \dot\rho_{\hat\beta}$ together with $\hat\sigma_j^2 = (\hat\Theta P_n \dot\rho_{\hat\beta}\dot\rho_{\hat\beta}^T \hat\Theta^T)_{j,j}$ and componentwise confidence intervals/$p$-values.
